newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S MANDELA TO MAKE CHINA STATEMENT-SOURCES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S MANDELA TO MAKE CHINA STATEMENT-SOURCES.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela will announce on Wednesday his government's future policy towards Taiwan, with which it has diplomatic ties, and China, with which it does not, government sources said.
Pretoria's ties with Taipei, inherited from the days of white minority rule, have angered Beijing which refuses to establish relations with any of the 30 countries that recognise Taiwan.
But Mandela said earlier this year it would be immoral for him to drop a country which had helped finance his African National Congress's (ANC) election campaign in 1994.

He said he wanted ties with both countries and urged Beijing and Taipei to sort out their differences themselves. Taiwan has major investments in South Africa but China offers huge trading opportunities.
Mandela sent his Foreign Minster Alfred Nzo to visit both Chinas this year and asked his ministry to compile a report on his findings which has not yet been made public.
Government and ANC sources confirmed that a news conference called by Mandela for four p.m. (1400 GMT) would be about China.
Taiwanese embassy officials said they had no knowledge of an impending announcement.
Beijing says it alone has the right to represent China. It has the one seat for China at the United Nations and is recognised by most major nations.
When the Communists took over mainland China after a civil war in 1949, the fleeing Nationalists set up a rival government on the island of Taiwan.
Beijing insists it should come under its own rule.
Taiwan's ambassador Loh I-Cheng said last month South Africa was dragging its feet on a proposed $3.5 billion petrochemicals complex joint venture mooted for the poor Eastern Cape province.
The project was proposed by Taiwanese vice premier Hsu Li-teh during an official visit in August.
A domestic consortium grouping Polifin, Sasol, Sentrachem and AECI was due to have responded to the proposals by the end of last month but is still mulling it over.
